A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same study. Their text, equations, tables, figures, and appendices support comparison, including matching material relocated into v3's expanded appendices.

before.justification: v1 reports original retrieval, memory-maintenance, question-answering, and efficiency experiments on LongMemEval and HaluMem.

after.justification: v3 retains original experiments and reports additional HaluMem configurations, ablations, question-type results, and qualitative cases.

M1.justification: The framework, graph constructions, and retrieval/reranking procedures are retained. Appendix C.3.3 first describes Prejudge filtering and states that it is used throughout the experiments, while most original results remain unchanged. Because v1 does not document this filtering, the PDFs do not establish whether it was newly introduced or previously used but undisclosed.

E1.justification: Original evaluations retain LongMemEval-S/M and HaluMem-Medium. The added retrieval measurements and question-type breakdowns examine existing coverage. HaluMem-Long results in Table C.2 are explicitly reproduced from the HaluMem paper, not newly evaluated by this work.

E2.justification: Table C.1 adds an edge-enabled grouped-key configuration to the HaluMem comparisons, alongside configurations without edges; this comparator was absent from v1's HaluMem tables. The named systems in Tables C.2 and D.2 are literature-result compilations, not documented reruns against the proposed configurations.

E3.justification: v3 adds HaluMem retrieval evaluation using constructed session-level ground truth, filtered/unfiltered assistant-question reporting, and API-model HaluMem configurations. Table C.1 also assigns session-inclusive key descriptions to maintenance results that v1 presented under a no-raw-key setting. This changes the reported experimental configuration without establishing that those experiments were rerun.

E4.justification: New analyses test removing Add while retaining Update/Noop, enabling versus disabling Prejudge, and HaluMem key organization (Tables C.5–C.7). Figure C.1 adds question-type breakdowns, and Figures E.1–E.5 provide graph success/failure and entity-name versus description cases. The efficiency analysis is retained and relocated, not newly added.

E5.justification: Both versions report point estimates without repeated-run counts, random-seed information, confidence intervals, or statistical tests. The added radar-chart lines represent configurations and filtering conditions, not uncertainty estimates.

E6.justification: Table 8's local flat configuration changes recall/precision/QA from 0.7124/0.9808/0.5535 to 0.8057/0.8846/0.5861. Earlier values reappear under session-inclusive labels in Table C.1, preventing an unqualified same-setting improvement claim. v3 also adds API HaluMem QA results of 0.5645 for flat and 0.6322 for graph, plus ablation and subtype results. LongMemEval Tables 2 and 4–7 retain their numerical results.

T1.justification: The six-tuple framework and mathematical descriptions of retrieval and ranking remain unchanged. Expanded terminology and relocated memory-operation definitions do not introduce new formal assumptions, derivations, theorems, or proofs.

C1.justification: The abstract narrows its attribution: v1 says performance differences arise from foundational settings rather than architectural innovations, whereas v3 asserts that implementation details substantially affect performance. The main contributions remain the unified framework, controlled comparisons, and strong baselines.

C2.justification: Section 4.3 reverses its explanation of maintenance operations from improved precision and reduced recall to improved recall and reduced precision. v3 qualifies the HaluMem graph disadvantage by extraction-model strength, explains assistant-question failures through user-only extraction and filtering, and adds case-based explanations of distraction and fragmented evidence. Limitations now explicitly address framework coverage and untested memory-management approaches.

D1.justification: v3 adds a code-access statement, the complete graph-extraction prompt, sources for extraction/answering/judging prompts, and the CoN-plus-JSON answering setting. It also documents judges, the five-session answering budget, aggregation scoring, user-only graph construction, and Prejudge filtering. These are substantial disclosures; the PDFs do not establish that each represents an implementation change.

R1.justification: Appendix D.2 adds a substantial comparison of published systems' settings and results, followed by claims of state-of-the-art performance and gains beyond backbone selection. This strengthens positioning relative to v1's stated aim of controlled analysis without identifying a single best system. Additional citations cover memory taxonomies, Nemori, graph retrieval, and reinforcement-learning-based memory management.

P1.justification: v3 substantially reorganizes supporting material: dataset exposition, memory-operation explanations, efficiency analysis, and system decomposition move into reorganized appendices. It rewrites key-organization terminology and experimental discussions, introduces explicit Takeaway paragraphs, and expands the limitations. These changes reshape the narrative beyond simply appending new results.

P2.justification: v3 adds the six-panel radar figure, five illustrated case comparisons, a full extraction-prompt panel, and several experimental and literature-comparison tables. Table 8 gains rows and a memory-update column. The efficiency table and system-decomposition table move from v1 Tables 9–10 to Tables C.4 and D.1.

improvement.justification: Added ablations, error analyses, prompts, and code-access information improve auditability. However, Table 7 specifies GPT-4o answering while Appendix C.1 and Table D.2 specify GPT-4o-mini, and D.2 claims superiority beyond backbone selection using heterogeneous published settings. The HaluMem configuration relabeling also remains unreconciled. These issues affect interpretation of central results, leaving the net quality benefit uncertain despite the useful additions.
